newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Finolex to hike PVC capacity.
newsitem.headline: India's Finolex to hike PVC capacity.

text.p: India's Finolex Industries Ltd will raise its polyvinyl chloride (PVC) manufacturing capacity to 200,000 tonnes per annum from 130,000 tonnes by 1998/99 (April-March), its chairman said on Monday.
"Today we are manufacturing 110,000 tonnes of the installed capacity," Finolex chairman Pralhad Chhabria told Reuters in the western Indian city of Pune where the firm is headquartered.
"We are expanding this by 1997/98 and 1998/99 from 130,000 tonnes to 200,000 tonnes," he said in an interview.
The company makes PVC from imported raw materials at its plant on the western coast of Ratnagiri.
"We foresee the demand of PVC in India crossing the one million tonnes-a-year mark soon," Chhabria said.
"So we are going to catch up again from 200,000 tonnes to 300,000 tonnes," he said without specifying when.
The company has received permission to build a captive 25 MW power plant at its PVC works, Chhabria said.
The expansion will be partly funded through offshore debt and the balance through internal accruals.
Finolex Industries has already raised $10 million debt and plans to raise another $30 million later in 1997/98, he said.
